rationale: The paper contributes distributed subset-selection algorithms for pairwise submodular objectives and a partition-based greedy procedure in a data-processing framework. These are data-selection and distributed algorithm contributions, not new kernels, fusion, precision formats, or kernel-level layouts.

The stated contributions are optimized software kernels for N:M-pruned convolution and fully connected layers on RISC-V MCUs, plus an ISA extension that accelerates sparse index decompression/activation decimation. The compiler integration uses those sparse kernels for full DNNs, squarely matching kernel-style sparse DNN optimization.

MiLo is an MoE quantization method for W3A16 inference and explicitly develops Tensor Core-friendly 3-bit GEMM kernels to turn extreme quantization into measured latency speedups. The low-rank compensators are algorithmic, but the paper includes kernel support as a central contribution.

FastTree proposes GPU attention kernels tailored to radix-tree KV-cache sharing and a runtime grouping heuristic to reduce redundant KV loads and improve tensor-core use. The evaluation centers on kernel speedups and end-to-end LLM serving throughput.

FedProphet is a federated adversarial training framework that partitions models into cascaded modules and coordinates training to reduce memory and inconsistency. Its contributions are training algorithms and FL orchestration rather than compute kernels or kernel-level formats.

LAVA contributes VM lifetime prediction, reprediction, and scheduling/defragmentation algorithms for cloud data-center placement. This is infrastructure scheduling and resource allocation above the kernel level.

JaxPP provides a programming model, task graph, and MPMD runtime for flexible pipeline-parallel training schedules. It composes distributed SPMD tasks but does not generate or optimize compute kernels under the codebook definition.

ScaleFusion accelerates distributed ST-DiT inference by scheduling all-to-all communication around spatial and temporal attention layers. The contribution is distributed communication scheduling for sequence parallelism rather than a new kernel, fusion kernel, or compiler/DSL outputting kernels.

Lumos is a trace-driven performance modeling and simulation toolkit for large-scale LLM training configurations. It models execution traces and estimates performance; it does not contribute kernels or kernel-level optimizations.

The paper recovers quality in structured-pruned LLMs by generating self-distilled fine-tuning data and using model merging/speculative decoding. This is model compression and fine-tuning without a kernel contribution.

DIP proposes predictor-free dynamic sparsification and cache-aware masking for on-device LLM inference, evaluated with a memory-transfer simulator. The work is a pruning/cache policy for model execution and does not present a new kernel implementation or kernel-level compiler output.

Bio-FO is a biologically plausible forward-only on-device learning algorithm evaluated on classification tasks and a Jetson Nano. The contribution is an alternative training algorithm, not a kernel-style optimization.
